To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fas is decreased in low-grade prostate cancer, is further decreased in high-grade cancer, and is absent in metastatic cancer.

1) Fas is expressed by basal epithelial cells of benign prostatic tissue; 2) Fas expression is decreased in low-grade and high-grade prostate cancer; and 3) Fas is absent in metastatic prostate cancer.

1) Fas expression is reduced in prostate cancer compared to benign prostate, 2) the reduction is inversely related to tumor grade, and 3) Fas expression in benign prostatic epithelum is predominantly secretory, whereas Fas expression in prostatic cancer is predominantly basal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms that lead to the development of prostatic carcinoma.
the molecular events in the progression from normal prostate to metastatic prostate cancer.
the study of the molecular mechanisms involved in prostate cancer progression and the development of new molecular markers and therapeutic approaches.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Fas receptor is expressed in normal prostate, and is decreased or lost in prostate cancer.
Fas is expressed on basal cells of the normal prostate and that its expression is lost in prostate cancer.
Fas expression is decreased and Bcl- 2 expression is increased in prostatic carcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of Fas and/or Bcl-2 may be useful in the evaluation of patients with prostate cancer.
decreased expression of FAS and over-expression of Bcl- 2 are molecular events that occur during the development of prostate cancer.
Fas is a tumor suppressor gene in prostate cancer and Bcl- 2 is an oncogene in this disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fas expression in the prostate is decreased in prostate cancer and this is an early event.
the Fas receptor is downregulated early in prostate cancer progression.
the expression of Fas is reduced and Bcl- 2 is overexpresses in prostate cancer, and these alterations are related to disease progression.
